headline: 140 kph winds: Cyclone Arnab to hit India on Wednesday
summary: India's eastern coast is preparing for a 'very severe cyclonic storm' with mass evacuations and school closures in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
details: Cyclone Arnab, which formed over the Bay of Bengal, is expected to make landfall in Andhra Pradesh, India, by Wednesday morning.
The India Meteorological Department reports that the storm will bring gusts of up to 140 kph (87 mph) and heavy to extremely heavy rainfall.
Andhra Pradesh has identified 570,000 vulnerable people and has begun evacuations to ensure safety before the storm hits.
The state government has also ordered all boats at sea to return to shore and mandated the speedy restoration of power in case of outages.
In neighboring Odisha, the government has closed schools and colleges in five districts for Tuesday and Wednesday.
Odisha officials are currently moving residents from low-lying areas into designated cyclone shelters to prevent casualties.
The Bay of Bengal is known as one of the world's most active regions for tropical cyclones, frequently impacting both India and Bangladesh.

headline_marked: Police will [[resort to crossfire if government allows]], says IGP
headline: Police will resort to crossfire if government allows, says IGP
summary: Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir stated that law enforcers will act according to the law and Constitution regardless of political changes.
details: Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir has stated that the police will resort to 'crossfire' where needed if the government provides the necessary authorization.
Speaking at a banking system launch in Dhaka’s Chawkbazar on Monday, the IGP emphasized that law enforcers will operate according to the law and the Constitution of Bangladesh.
He addressed criticisms of the force, noting that police are often branded as 'fascist' when using batons but are viewed as weak when they remain silent.
The IGP argued that there is no substitute for the police force in maintaining peace and order, and urged the public not to take the law into their own hands.
He also raised concerns over the spread of drugs in neighborhoods, alleging that some police personnel were involved in drug trafficking alongside members of the ousted Awami League.
According to the IGP, 27 police members have been suspended over the past two months due to their alleged involvement in drug-related activities.
caption:

He addressed criticisms of the force, noting that police are often branded as 'fascist' when using batons but are viewed as weak when they remain silent.

He also raised concerns over the spread of drugs in neighborhoods, alleging that some police personnel were involved in drug trafficking alongside members of the ousted Awami League.
